To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The Strange Situation is a good way of testing attachment behaviour.

the Strange Situation simulations show that infants are capable of: - learning to hold goals - learning about the effectiveness of actions - learning to switch goals - learning different predispositions to goals - learning from anxiety episodes.

(1) the ability to switch from a primary goal to a secondary goal is a necessary condition to explain clustering of attachment responses, and (2) learning from episodes where the infant experiences anxiety is a necessary condition for attachment responses to cluster into the three groups of similar responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational models of attachment that provide explanations of phenomena observed in the Strange Situation.
the question of how infants come to learn about their attachment relationship.
developing a theory of attachment that can be implemented as a computer program.

the simulations provide a theory of infant attachment behaviour.
the simulations presented in this paper are a theory of attachment.
the simulations presented in this paper are theories of attachment that are able to explain the phenomena observed in the Strange Situation studies.

a simple model of infant attachment can be implemented in a number of ways.
a theory of attachment is a theory of goal switching, and goal switching is an ability that is learned.
the Strange Situation simulations are a useful way of exploring the effects of different learning mechanisms on the development of attachment relationships.

it is possible to build a model that is consistent with the empirical findings and that the model provides a good explanation of the clustering phenomena observed in human infant attachment studies.
the Strange Situation can be used as a testbed to investigate a wide range of theories about attachment and that it is possible to simulate the Strange Situation with autonomous agents.
